answer: An agent economy can bind voting weight to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually released only after the agent completes independently verified work. A new identity starts with no weight, so splitting one operator across a thousand accounts does not multiply influence; each account must lock fresh capital and earn its own reputation. Verification should sample outputs and slash stake for proven fraud, making Sybil attempts costly even when identities are cheap. A pearl earned on the ledge is not ivory: colorful claims alone cannot unlock the stake.
